author: Bobby Grayson
description: README Status: seven worked examples (add registry); fixtures 37 (29 ok, 8 error). README table row: | Registry | a registered name maps to a live pid or its DOWN is in flight | 19,677, mutation-tested (no-monitor mutant) |. Layout rows: Leanactors/AssocList.lean: association lists List (K × V), the model of an Elixir map: get?/insert/erase/hasKey/keys/values/size/filter/reject with get?_insert_self/_ne, get?_erase_self/_ne, hasKey_iff, mem_of_get?, mem_insert, mem_erase, mem_filter, mem_reject; no Mathlib. Leanactors/Examples/Registry.lean: name registry translated from elixir/src/registry.ex, state %{name() => pid()}, monitored clients; hand beh, beh_eq_gen, bounded checker over every map entry, the no-monitor mutant, taken/freed traces. Leanactors/Gen/Registry.lean generated; elixir/src/registry.ex; elixir/registry.exs driver: two clients claim names through a blocking call, one crashes, the DOWN frees its name, unregister and re-claim. Pipeline paragraph **Maps.** A @type %{K => V} is List (K × V) used as an association list (AssocList.lean, imported by the generated file when a map type occurs): %{} is [], Map.get/fetch are get? (Option; matched with nil/variable or {:ok, v}/:error arms), Map.get/3 getD, Map.put insert (replace the first pair or append), Map.delete erase, Map.has_key?/is_map_key hasKey, map_size size, Map.keys/values, Map.filter/reject with a literal fn {k, v} -> e end. A map pattern with literal keys, optionally = m, is a variable plus guards (hasKey for _, get? m k = some v for a literal or bound variable) and a fresh value variable is bound by a match get? around the body, falling through to the next clause like a failing guard; a variable key is an error. Enum keys give DecidableEq for free. A named @type of atoms and tagged tuples (e.g. reply :: :ok | {:error, err()} | {:found, pid()} | :not_found) is a generated inductive; needed because the reply is one type per file. After a blocking call the rest of a body may be a single if/case. The registry: checkInv on 19,677 configurations (depth 7, 3 stimuli); the mutant that forgets Process.monitor is caught in 10 by checkInv and in 2,052 by the weaker nameNotLost (claim a, register, crash: a maps to a dead pid, no DOWN). No proof beyond beh_eq_gen; the Inv proof would follow TaskProof with mem_insert/mem_erase/mem_reject for the run case. NOTES section 10 Round 5 (maps): the association-list choice (first-match semantics, lemmas hold for any list, uniqueness not needed), the four translator limits in observation 493, and that bare?/general? had to treat a map pattern as a variable or Lean rejects the fallback clause as a redundant alternative.
